newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn stands firm on solidarity tax cut-Waigel.
newsitem.headline: Bonn stands firm on solidarity tax cut-Waigel.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said on Monday that Bonn would stand by its plan to cut a unification tax surcharge to 5.5 percent from 7.5 percent on January 1, 1998.
"On this net reduction of 7.5 billion marks, which will help consumers and investment and support the recovery, we stand firm," he said at a conference of tax advisers in this northern coastal town.
But Peter Hintze, general secretary of Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democratic party (CDU), said the coalition still had to discuss a reduction of the solidarity tax.
Over the weekend, Waigel told newsweekly Der Spiegel that tax increases were not ruled out in the effort to close Germany's budget deficit.
